claim: AAAI reviewers are explicitly instructed to check whether the empirical evaluation includes appropriate baselines and comparisons to validate the proposed approach against the state of the art.
stance_target: what the AAAI acceptance bar requires empirically
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track, applies to AAAI-27 by continuity of process
quoted_support: Does the empirical evaluation include appropriate baselines and comparisons to validate the proposed approach compared to the state of the art?

claim: AAAI reviewers are instructed to check whether the paper includes an analysis of errors made by the proposed approach, not just aggregate performance numbers.
stance_target: what the AAAI acceptance bar requires empirically
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track reviewer checklist
quoted_support: Does the paper include an analysis of errors made by the proposed approach?

claim: AAAI reviewers are asked whether better benchmarks or datasets should have been used, meaning benchmark choice itself is scored, not just performance on the chosen benchmark.
stance_target: what the AAAI acceptance bar requires empirically
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track reviewer checklist
quoted_support: Are the evaluation benchmarks and datasets appropriately chosen? Are there any better benchmarks or datasets that should have been used?

claim: Reviewers are instructed to check full replicability of evaluations as a distinct criterion from whether results support claims.
stance_target: what the AAAI acceptance bar requires for reproducibility
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track reviewer checklist

claim: Phase 1 AAAI review includes an AI-generated review alongside two human reviews, but the AI review carries no rating or recommendation and cannot itself advance or reject a paper -- only human ratings decide Phase 1 progression.
stance_target: role of AI in the AAAI acceptance decision
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 two-phase review process, continued into AAAI-27
quoted_support: This AI review will not include any ratings or recommendations... Only the human-written reviews and human expertise will be used to decide whether the paper proceeds to Phase 2.

claim: Reviewers are guided to ask whether the key novel technical contribution is clear and whether the paper's limitations in scope and generalizability are clearly described, treating explicit limitation-statement as a scored positive rather than a weakness to hide.
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track reviewer checklist
quoted_support: Does the paper clearly describe the limitations (in scope and generalizability) of its conclusions? (All work has limits, and it is vital to understand them.)
